instrucciones: For questions 25–30, complete the second sentence so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence, using the word given. Do not change the word given. You must use between three and six words, including the word given.

items.frase: The beekeeper had barely opened the hive when the bees began to swarm out.
items.fin: the hive than the bees began to swarm out.
items.explicacion: "No sooner … than" with a negative adverbial at the start requires inversion: "No sooner had the beekeeper opened the hive than…".

items.frase: I regret not learning to play an instrument when I was younger.
items.fin: to play an instrument when I was younger.
items.explicacion: A regret about the past: "wish + past perfect".

items.frase: A local joiner repaired our front door last week.
items.fin: by a local joiner last week.
items.explicacion: Causative: "have + object + past participle" for a service done by someone else.

items.frase: I'm sure the museum was very busy because the car park was full.
items.fin: very busy because the car park was full.
items.explicacion: Deduction about the past: "must have + past participle".

items.frase: She invented an excuse so that she wouldn't have to attend the meeting.
items.fin: an excuse so that she wouldn't have to attend the meeting.
items.explicacion: "Make up" an excuse = invent one. Note: "came up with" and "thought up" also work but "made up" uses the key word.

items.frase: The journey took far more time than the guidebook had suggested.
items.explicacion: Comparative of "long": "much / far longer than" expresses a big difference.
